title: If You're Defending Education Against AI, You Don't Understand Learning
author: Patrick Dempsey
summary: Four words used interchangeably in education — learning, teaching, school, and education — originally implied motion and aliveness. Over time they were collapsed into a single system focused on credentialing. When people panic about AI threatening 'education,' they are actually defending the credential, the homework, and the essay — not learning itself. AI didn't create the misalignment between the system and genuine learning; it just made the problem impossible to ignore.
points: Learning (Old English: follow a track), teaching (to show; walk alongside), school (leisure/contemplative time), education (to lead out/draw forth) — all implied motion and aliveness at their roots.
The modern school has become a credentialing processor; teaching has become transmission; learning has been reduced to getting the correct answer on a test.
The conflation of all four words into 'education' makes AI discussions confusing — defenders are protecting the system, not learning.
Learning is fundamental to being human: you cannot not learn. Even resisting the system is learning.
If you removed education, school, and teaching entirely, learning would still happen — it has to.
The system is worth something when it serves learning; it stops being worth something when it starts serving itself.
AI didn't create the problem that education measures how well a student's brain adapted to an environment engineered against how brains actually work.
quotes: Modern education measures how well a student's brain has adapted to an environment specifically engineered against how human brains actually encode and retrieve information.
What we're really defending, when we panic about AI, is the word education. The educational system. We've taken it to be essential to learning. In many ways it isn't.
AI didn't create the problem, but it made it impossible to ignore.
